To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the herbicides hexazinone and diuron, when applied at concentrations typically found in aquatic ecosystems, can have long‐term negative effects on the abundance and community structure of phytoplankton and zooplankton and can negatively affect the abundance of some macroinvertebrates.

1) herbicides can have direct and indirect effects on phytoplankton and other aquatic organisms, 2) herbicide applications altered the relative abundance and community structure of phytoplankton communities, 3) herbicide applications had no effect on the abundance of zooplankton, and 4) herbicide applications reduced the abundance and diversity of macroinvertebrate communities.

(i) herbicides have the potential to alter phytoplankton and macroinvertebrate communities in aquatic ecosystems, (ii) herbicides can have indirect effects on higher‐level consumers through their effects on primary producers, and (iii) long‐term exposures to herbicides are more likely to elicit effects than short‐term exposures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of pesticides on freshwater ecosystems.
understanding the ecological consequences of herbicides in aquatic systems.
the direct and indirect effects that herbicides may have on aquatic communities.

the herbicides diurone and hexazinon can cause direct effects in aquatic organisms, and that these effects can be transferred to the higher trophic levels in the aquatic food webs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
herbicide mixtures have a significant impact on phytoplankton communities and that the effects are not additive.

herbicide applications can have significant effects on aquatic community structure, but the magnitude of these effects depends on herbicide type, concentration and timing, and the species composition of the community at the time of application.
herbicide exposure can alter the structure of aquatic food webs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can predict how herbicides will impact the aquatic communities by looking at how they impact phytoplankton and zooplankton.
the effects of herbicides on aquatic ecosystems can be more complex than previously recognized.
the effects of herbicides on the aquatic community may be more complex than what is typically assessed in risk assessment studies.
